history.summary: ISKCON's Noida temple, formerly/also known as the Sri Sri Radha Govind Temple, was founded by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness in 1998 on a 2-acre plot at Sector 33, Noida. The Gaudiya Vaishnava temple houses Radha-Krishna as Sri Sri Radha Govind and has a meditation centre, Vedic museum, Vrindavan garden, and Govinda's vegetarian restaurant; weekly Harinam Sankirtan is held on Saturdays. Entry is free. Opening hours conflict between sources: most list 4:30 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-8:30 PM; a few list 4:30 AM-9:00 PM or 10:00 AM-1:00 PM for the morning session (verify).

name: ISKCON Temple Noida
town_description: Noida (New Okhla Industrial Development Authority) is a planned city in Gautam Buddha Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, on the eastern edge of the National Capital Region. Developed from the late 1970s as an industrial township across the Yamuna from Delhi, it is now a major hub for IT, media, and manufacturing, with wide avenues, metro connectivity, and a large Bengali, south Indian, and pan-Indian migrant population that sustains many community temples.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~30 km)
travel.railway: Noida has no mainline station; nearest: New Delhi / Hazrat Nizamuddin (~20 km)
travel.road: A-5, Maharaja Agrasen Marg, Sector 33; nearest metro: Noida City Centre / Sector 18 (Blue Line), then auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami (August/September) is the grandest festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-8:30 PM daily (sources conflict; verify before visiting)
